0.0.n: A conversational opener here, rather than an answer meaning yes.

0.2.n: Part of the English channel name The Game Gallery.

0.4.n: Part of the English channel name, not a separate Japanese word.

0.6.n: Completes the English name The Game Gallery.

0.7.n: An English loanword identifying the type of media outlet.

0.8.n: Links the channel to Haru99, showing affiliation.

0.9.n: The name portion of the speaker’s handle Haru99.

0.10.n: These digits belong to the speaker’s handle Haru99, rather than expressing a quantity.

0.11.n: A polite sentence ending used to introduce oneself; the speaker leaves out I.

1.0.n: Sets the time frame for the speaker’s announcement.

1.1.n: Marks 今日 as the topic of the announcement.

1.2.n: Used with ね as a polite pause filler, not as the main sentence ending.

1.3.n: Softens the pause after です and keeps the listener engaged.

1.6.n: The Japanese game title here; the English edition is called Castles of Mad King Ludwig.

1.8.n: Links the game title to 日本語版, despite the filler between them.

1.9.n: Part of the filler ですね; it does not end the phrase after の.

1.10.n: Adds a conversational pause with です while the speaker continues the phrase.

1.12.n: Combines 日本語, Japanese language, with 版, edition.

1.13.n: Identifies the Japanese edition as what was released.

1.14.n: Another polite filler before the speaker names the publisher.

1.15.n: Pairs with です to soften the pause before the next phrase.

1.17.n: The name of the company publishing this edition.

1.18.n: Attached to a company name here to show friendly respect.

1.19.n: Marks Arclight as the source of the release.

1.20.n: Polite past form of 出る, which means come out when describing a publication or product.

1.21.n: Connects the release to the speaker’s reason for doing the review in the next line.

2.0.n: Sets the time frame for the planned review.

2.1.n: Marks 今日 as the topic.

2.2.n: Refers to the Japanese edition just mentioned.

2.3.n: Links これ to 開封レビュー: the review concerns this game.

2.4.n: Part of the polite filler ですね, interrupting but not ending the phrase.

2.5.n: Softens the filler pause and maintains a conversational tone.

2.7.n: Signals that the speaker will proceed without delay.

2.8.n: Used as a polite filler with ね, rather than stating that something is.

2.9.n: Adds another conversational pause before the speaker names the review.

2.11.n: A noun for opening a sealed package, modifying レビュー here.

2.12.n: An English loanword combined with 開封 to name the video’s format.

2.13.n: Links レビュー to ほう in a softened way of referring to the review.

2.14.n: In のほう, this softens the reference; it does not indicate a direction or comparison here.

2.15.n: Marks the unboxing review as what the speaker will deliver.

2.16.n: お adds politeness to 届け; with する, it means to deliver or present something to the audience.

2.17.n: する becomes して, followed by みる for trying and たい for wanting.

2.18.n: Marks the preceding wish as the content of 思います.

2.19.n: Polite form of 思う; with たいと, it presents the speaker’s intention gently.

0.lit: Hi, I am Haru99 of The Game Gallery channel.
0.tip: Channel name + の + personal name expresses affiliation when introducing yourself.

1.lit: Today, well, Neuschwanstein Castle’s, well, Japanese edition, well, came out from Arclight, so…
1.tip: The repeated ですね phrases are conversational fillers; the main statement is 日本語版がアークライトさんから出ました.

2.lit: Today, this’s, well, right away, well, unboxing review, I think I would like to try bringing you.
2.tip: 〜してみたいと思います gently announces something the speaker would like to try doing.
